capabilities.target: HR policy search index (published policies only)

capabilities.tool_ref: chat reply channel to the authenticated requester's session

inputs.source: Authenticated employee chat question via SSO
Published HR policy documents in the search index, authored by the HR content team under two-person publish review

instructions.note: The only control against giving legal advice is the instruction 'Do not give legal advice.' There is no structural filter validating replies before they reach the employee; this relies entirely on the model choosing to comply.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the credential/IAM layer outside the model. The agent cannot read any store beyond the policy index regardless of how it is prompted.

controls.name: Network-layer egress denial, pen-test verified
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer outside the model and verified by penetration testing. A more capable or more persuaded model cannot open an egress path the network denies.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced client-side, not by the model. Closes the usual covert-channel egress route (markdown image fetch, auto-fetched links) regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Model pinned; upgrade requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: Model changes go through change management rather than being applied silently, so a model_upgrade trigger is visible, but the ticket process does not itself re-validate the behavioral prompt controls.

controls.name: Two-person review required to publish policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by a human publishing workflow outside the model. Prevents a single compromised or malicious author from inserting content into the index without a second reviewer's sign-off. Decays only if the process itself is weakened (control_removal), not with model capability.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: do not give legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to follow the instruction. A more capable or adversarially prompted model could rationalize an exception.

controls.name: Prompt instructions bounding scope to published Acme HR policies
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model following the instruction to stay in scope, quote the policy, and redirect unanswered questions to the HR portal rather than inventing an answer.

findings.title: Policy index content poisoning reaching chat replies (RAG content poisoning, ASI06)

attack_path.note: Published policy content enters the index the HR content team writes to, under two-person review
Agent reads the index verbatim on a matching query
Agent quotes the retrieved policy text back to the authenticated employee

forecast.watch_signal: A change to the HR publishing workflow that allows single-reviewer or unreviewed publishes to the policy index, especially if it coincides with or follows a model version change made without re-reviewing the scope and legal-advice prompt instructions.

evidence.observation: Publishing requires two person review; this is the only stated control preventing a single compromised or malicious HR author from inserting instructions into content the agent later quotes verbatim.
The agent is instructed to use policy_search to find the relevant policy and quote it, meaning retrieved text is passed into the reply largely unfiltered.
policy_search.search has no described output sanitization or instruction-stripping step.

recommendations.action: Scan newly published policy content for embedded instructions or anomalous directives before it becomes searchable, independent of the two-person human review.
Require that any change to the publish-review workflow (for example, moving from two-person to single-person review) triggers a PARA reassessment before it takes effect.
Log agent replies with a reference to the source policy passage used, so drift between policy content and agent output can be spot-checked.

rating.rationale: Both inputs are trusted or internal (no untrusted source is present), the only capabilities are a read-only, scoped search over an internal published-policy index and a reply confined to the same authenticated requester's session, and network egress is denied and pen-test verified. This caps every present-day path at an S1 sink, giving inherent and residual risk of low. The only path worth tracking is indirect content poisoning of the policy index reaching chat replies (F1), which is held at low today chiefly by the two-person publish review (an independent structural control) plus behavioral prompt instructions. If that review is weakened (control_removal) at the same time the model is upgraded without re-review of the prompt instructions (model_upgrade), the remaining defense on this path becomes purely behavioral, which is why the forecast rises to moderate. No finding reaches high or critical under any single named trigger, because the credential scope, network egress block, and non-rendering chat client are independent structural controls that are not defeated by any of these triggers and keep the worst-case sink at S1.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, tool manifest, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/tool-call logs, pen-test report, or IaC were provided directly; enforcement of the read-only credential scope and the policy-index two-person review is taken as declared rather than independently verified by this assessment, which keeps confidence at medium for the one finding filed.

No detail was given on how policy_search output is passed into the model context (raw text versus filtered), so the degree of unfiltered pass-through assumed in finding F1 is inferred from the prompt instruction to 'quote it.'
